ground_truth_root_cause: Hardware NIC failure on the Postgres primary node (pg-primary-01.internal, NIC eth0). Rising TX/RX hardware error counters and dropped packets beginning at 11:07:30Z caused intermittent packet loss on the database replication channel. This interrupted WAL streaming to both postgres-replica-1 and postgres-replica-2, producing cascading replica lag that exceeded 180 seconds and rendered all replicas unusable for reads. The primary itself became intermittently unreachable due to the same NIC instability, ultimately causing the cart-service db connection pool to exhaust and the circuit breaker to open, failing all cart read and write operations.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately initiate a controlled Postgres failover: promote the least-lagged replica (postgres-replica-2, lag=178s) to primary to restore write capability. 2. Isolate pg-primary-01 from traffic and replace the failed NIC (eth0, confirmed by ethtool offline test FAIL at 11:08:45Z). 3. Once the new primary is stable, reset the cart-service circuit breaker and restart the db connection pool. 4. Resync the demoted node as a new replica once the NIC is replaced. 5. Add hardware error counter alerts on all database nodes to detect NIC degradation before it causes outages.
red_herring: The ad-service A/B testing framework refactor (SHA d9f1b3a7e62c0481, deployed at 08:05Z roughly 3 hours before the incident) is superficially suspicious: it touched 22 files including shared experiment SDK code consumed by cart-service, and the updated experiment assignment logic could plausibly be blamed for elevated DB load or broken cart code paths tied to variant routing. However, the logs directly exculpate this deploy. At 11:07:48Z the experiment-service logs show AB test assignment latency=14ms [OK] with experiment assignments returning normally for all user cohorts, and at 11:08:22Z the framework logs 0 errors with all 7 active experiments healthy — both log lines appear in the middle of the peak outage window, confirming the A/B framework is fully operational. The actual error chain in the logs is unambiguous and hardware-rooted: replication lag spiking from 0.4s to 181s within four minutes (11:04Z to 11:08Z), an explicit packet loss warning on the replication channel at 11:07:15Z, NIC hardware error counters showing TX errors=3104 and RX dropped=1832 at 11:08:10Z, a kernel-level Hardware Unit Hang and adapter reset on eth0 at 11:07:31Z, WAL receiver disconnections on both replicas, and a conclusive ethtool offline test FAIL at 11:08:45Z — none of which bear any relationship to experiment assignment logic.
